Definition: a prolonged form of a primary verb, which is used only as an alternate in certain tenses; to lie hid (literally or figuratively); often used adverbially, unwittingly:--be hid, be ignorant of, unawares.
BiblicalUsage: To escape notice is to lie hidden, and the word is used for ignorance both wilful and unknowing. In 2 Peter 3:5 the scoffers "willingly are ignorant" of the creation and the flood, in Hebrews 13:2 some "have entertained angels unawares," and in Luke 8:47 the woman who touched Jesus saw "she was not hid" and came trembling to tell all.
TheologicalSignificance: I take it that the word draws the line between the two hidings: the scoffer hides the truth from himself on purpose, and the believer hides nothing, because nothing is hid from Him. One hiding is wilful blindness, and the other is no hiding at all.
